case_studies.observation: Baseline spatial representation remained consistent under compression, while frequency spectrum suffered degradation that lowered fusion confidence.
Spatial perturbations drifted ConvNeXt prediction, but multimodal FFT representation grounded the decision, maintaining high fusion stability.
Both architectures decisively recognized salient features that persisted across all degradation transforms.
Subtle boundary features were distorted by recompression and downsampling, inducing high probability drift and prediction flips across both models.

recommendation.state: C. Baseline and Fusion are similar in overall robustness
recommendation.rationale: Both architectures exhibit close average degraded AUC (0.9769 vs. 0.9754) and similar average flip rates (14.64% vs. 14.34%).
